notes.text: Use the large pot instead of the saucepan, so the rice cooks in a thin, even layer.

move.title: Toast it first
move.body: A pilaf is rice toasted in fat before any liquid goes in, then cooked in hot broth with the lid on. Turkish cooks toast a handful of orzo in butter first, until it's golden. Today you'll rinse the rice, toast it with the orzo, add hot broth, and leave the lid alone, so every grain comes out separate and fluffy.

callback.body: In jambalaya, rice cooked right in the broth in the pot, with the lid on and no stirring. A pilaf works the same way, with one step added: the rice is toasted in butter before the broth goes in.

why.title: Rinse until the water runs clearer
why.body: Dry rice is dusted with loose starch. Left on, it turns the cooking liquid gluey and sticks the grains together. Rinsed off, the grains stay separate.

why.title: Toasting coats and seals each grain
why.body: Stirred in hot butter, each grain gets a thin coat of fat and a lightly toasted outside. The coat keeps the grains from sticking to each other, and the toasting adds a nutty flavor plain rice doesn't have.

why.title: Hot broth
why.body: Hot broth keeps the pan at a boil, so the rice starts cooking evenly right away. Cold broth would stop it and leave the bottom grains soft and the top ones hard.

why.title: Lid on, hands off
why.body: The rice finishes cooking in the steam trapped under the lid. Lift it and the steam escapes; stir it and the grains break and turn sticky. Set the timer and leave it.

why.title: Let it rest
why.body: Off the heat with the lid on, the last of the steam soaks into the grains evenly, and they firm up. Fluffed right away, the top is wet and the bottom is soft.

wrong.sign: The rice is crunchy when the timer rings
wrong.fix: Sprinkle 2 tablespoons of hot water over the top, put the lid back on, and cook 5 more minutes on low.
The rice wasn't rinsed enough, or it got stirred after the lid went on. It still tastes good; next time rinse well and leave it alone.
The heat was too high. If it smells burnt, start the orzo again; a light golden brown is the goal.
The heat was too high under the lid. Use your lowest burner setting next time.

quiz.q: What makes a pilaf different from plain boiled rice?
choices: The rice is toasted in fat before the liquid goes in
quiz.explain: The fat coats each grain and adds a nutty flavor.

quiz.q: Why does the broth go in hot?
choices: So the rice starts cooking evenly right away

quiz.q: Why let the rice rest before fluffing it?
choices: The last steam soaks in evenly and the grains firm up
quiz.explain: Fluffed too early, the top is wet.

steps.text: Put the rice in the medium bowl and cover it with cold water. Swish it with your hand, then carefully pour off the cloudy water, holding the rice back with your hand. Do this 4 or 5 times, until the water is only a little cloudy. Pour off as much water as you can.
steps.tip: Let it sit and drain while you heat the broth. A little water left behind is fine.

steps.text: Pour the broth into the liquid measuring cup and heat it in the microwave until it's steaming. Leave it in the microwave for now.
steps.tip: Use oven mitts to lift it out. The handle gets hot.

steps.text: Melt the butter in the saucepan over medium heat. If you're using the orzo, add it and stir until it's golden brown.
steps.look: Golden brown, like toast, not dark.

steps.text: Add the rice and stir it in the butter, scraping the bottom, until the grains look a little see-through at the edges and smell nutty.
steps.look: The grains are glossy and their edges have turned clear, with a white dot in the middle.

steps.text: With oven mitts, stand back and pour in the hot broth. It will sizzle and steam. Add the salt and pepper and stir once.
Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to your lowest setting and put the lid on. Cook without lifting the lid or stirring.
Turn off the burner and leave the lid on. Let the pilaf rest.
Take off the lid and fluff the rice gently with the fork, lifting from the bottom. Taste it and add a pinch more salt if it needs it.
steps.look: Every grain is separate and tender, with no water left in the pan.
